task: Implement TOTP and AAL2 workforce identity primitives in the canonical identity authority.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Workforce MFA primitives influence future privileged access decisions, so policy, factor counting, fail-closed evidence loading and use of the existing Supabase MFA authority must be proven before enforcement is wired into active admin access.

acceptanceCriteria: Platform owner policy requires two verified TOTP factors before future AAL2 enforcement can consider the owner ready.
Platform admin and merchant owner/admin policy requires one verified TOTP factor and AAL2.
Low-risk workforce roles are not globally MFA-blocked unless a caller explicitly marks the operation as a sensitive boundary.
Server assurance evidence fails closed when Supabase MFA state cannot be loaded.
Client primitives use the existing Supabase TOTP factor authority and do not persist a second OTP secret or verification authority.
This foundation does not yet change active admin routing or authorization behavior.
invariants: Supabase Auth remains the only MFA factor and authenticator assurance authority.
An AAL2 session cannot compensate for a missing required verified TOTP factor count.
A required verified factor count cannot compensate for a current session below AAL2.
Platform owner readiness is stricter than ordinary platform admin readiness.
Customer MFA policy is not changed by this workforce-only transaction.

failureModes: A platform owner reaches future privileged access with only one verified factor.
An existing verified factor is mistaken for current AAL2 after session assurance has dropped to AAL1.
An MFA API error is interpreted as no MFA requirement instead of unavailable assurance evidence.
A second local OTP store diverges from Supabase Auth and becomes an alternate authentication authority.
Low-risk staff are blocked globally even when they never cross a sensitive operation boundary.
Unverified or abandoned TOTP enrollment is counted as a verified factor.
edgeCases: A platform owner has one verified factor and an AAL2 session: the next step is enrollment of factor two, not ready.
A platform owner has two verified factors but an AAL1 session: the next step is challenge, not ready.
A merchant admin has one verified factor and AAL2: the policy can report ready.
A support user has no MFA and no sensitive boundary: the policy requires zero factors.
A support user crosses a security boundary: the policy requires one factor.
MFA state retrieval throws before either AAL or factor data is available: server snapshot remains unavailable and not ready.

alternatives.summary: Use Supabase Auth MFA as the single factor authority and add deterministic Shoperation workforce policy around it.
alternatives.reason: It preserves the existing authentication authority, avoids duplicate secret storage and gives the later enforcement layer a testable factor/AAL contract.

alternatives.summary: Let each login or admin UI decide factor requirements directly while calling Supabase MFA.
alternatives.reason: It would duplicate policy across surfaces and allow UI state to become an authorization authority.

alternatives.summary: Store Shoperation-owned TOTP secrets and verify codes in a separate first-party MFA service.
alternatives.reason: It creates a second authentication authority, expands secret-handling risk and conflicts with the one-canonical-authority architecture.

challenge.scenario: Platform owner has an AAL2 session but only one verified TOTP factor.
challenge.finding: Session AAL alone would incorrectly satisfy the stronger owner policy.
challenge.resolution: Readiness requires both current AAL2 and at least two verified TOTP factors for owner policy.

challenge.scenario: User has verified TOTP factors but the current session is AAL1.
challenge.finding: Enrollment history does not prove that the current session completed MFA.
challenge.resolution: The state model returns challenge until the current authenticator assurance level is AAL2.

challenge.scenario: Supabase MFA factor or AAL retrieval returns an error.
challenge.finding: Treating missing evidence as zero requirement would fail open.
challenge.resolution: Server assurance returns available=false and can never satisfy a positive factor requirement.

challenge.scenario: A low-risk viewer or support worker uses ordinary read/support operations.
challenge.finding: Global MFA enforcement would exceed the accepted PO policy and unnecessarily block routine work.
challenge.resolution: Low-risk roles require zero factors unless a sensitive boundary is explicitly requested.

challenge.scenario: A TOTP enrollment exists but is not verified.
challenge.finding: Counting enrollment existence would allow an abandoned factor to satisfy policy.
challenge.resolution: Only factors whose Supabase status is verified count toward the required factor total.

challenge.scenario: A future sensitive refund, provider credential or integration operation is performed by a normally low-risk actor.
challenge.finding: Role-level policy alone cannot express step-up authentication at a specific sensitive boundary.
challenge.resolution: The policy accepts an explicit sensitive boundary that raises the requirement to one verified factor/AAL2 without globally changing the role.

specialistReviews.finding: MFA factor truth must remain inside the existing identity authority and must not be duplicated in storefront or admin presentation code.
specialistReviews.resolution: The foundation lives only under src/lib/auth and wraps Supabase MFA without creating a new persistence authority.

specialistReviews.finding: AAL2 alone is insufficient for the accepted platform-owner two-factor enrollment rule, and provider failures must not silently downgrade assurance.
specialistReviews.resolution: Readiness checks both AAL2 and verified-factor count; server retrieval errors produce an unavailable fail-closed snapshot.

specialistReviews.finding: Putting MFA rules directly into later UI would repeat the known second-authority failure class and make route-specific behavior drift likely.
specialistReviews.resolution: Expose shared deterministic primitives now and keep later UI as a consumer of this identity authority.

proofPlan: Run deterministic policy tests for owner/admin/low-risk/sensitive-boundary factor requirements.
Run state-transition tests for enroll, challenge and ready decisions across AAL1/AAL2 and one/two-factor states.
Verify server assurance source fails closed on MFA retrieval failure and requires both AAL2 and factor count.
Verify client primitives call Supabase TOTP enrollment, factor listing and challengeAndVerify without browser secret persistence.
Run exact-head quality tests, TypeScript and production build before any enforcement wiring is allowed.

requirements.requirement: The canonical identity authority contains deterministic workforce TOTP/AAL2 policy and Supabase MFA primitives without yet changing active admin authorization enforcement.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The foundation must not create custom OTP secret persistence or a second MFA verification authority.
The foundation must not make customer MFA mandatory or globally require MFA for every low-risk workforce role.

notes: Stage 1 identity foundation only. This commit adds canonical policy and Supabase MFA primitives but deliberately does not alter active admin routing, middleware, authorization checks or customer authentication.
